text:
alex_support: folks, customer (maria) reporting streaming responses drop ~65s in, client sees partial final chunk then connection closes. They see many reconnects and billing spike.

maria_cust: repro steps: open SSE stream to /v1/stream?session=abc, after ~1m the stream stops sending events but TCP stays ESTABLISHED for another ~30s then client reconnects.

alex_support: got their request id header: x-rw-req-id=rw-9f3b, Cloudflare Ray: 7a1c2b3d4e, ALB request-id: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:req/0a1b2c.

josh_eng_runtime: can you paste the curl repro?

maria_cust: sure — curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-lite" and leave it running. I see data then a final `data: [partial]` line then nothing.

priya_sre: quick hypothesis: ALB idle timeout is 60s, our origin keepalive is 90s -> half-close race. Cloudflare sits in front which might do HTTP/2 multiplexing to ALB. Sometimes the ALB half-closes and Cloudflare still has an open HTTP/2 stream causing truncated chunks.

alex_support: customer is on Cloudflare-proxied domain (they confirmed). They also reported the issue happens more with long pauses between events (chat-like typing).

josh_eng_runtime: requests routed over HTTP/2 from Cloudflare to ALB can hide ALB FIN because CF maintains the stream. If ALB closes backend conn due to idle timeout, our origin may try to continue writing to closed socket -> partial chunk. Need pcap showing FIN sequence.

maria_cust: attached a tcpdump pcap (they uploaded to support ticket): I see FIN from 10.0.2.14 at 65.3s, then FIN-ACK, then retransmits.

priya_sre: can you also grab the ALB access logs window around the req id? want to see backend_status_code and termination_reason.

alex_support: requested logs, customer shared partial ALB entry: target_status_code=504, "reason":"Idle connection timed out".

josh_eng_runtime: that matches. Root cause likely mismatch between CF->ALB idle and our runtime's keepalive/streaming heartbeat. Two mitigations: (1) send more frequent SSE keepalive heartbeats when event gaps exceed 30s, (2) align ALB idle timeout to be > origin write window (set to 120s) or enable TCP keepalives.

priya_sre: quick workaround for customer: put a small periodic comment event every 20s from the app: `: keepalive\n\n` (just a colon-style SSE comment) — CF will forward as data and keep ALB busy. Ask them to try and report.

maria_cust: trying comment keepalive now, will report back in 3min.

alex_support: also asked them to toggle Cloudflare "Origin Keepalive Timeout" and to try direct-to-origin bypass (dev subdomain) to see if CF is contributing.

cf-bot: Cloudflare: Observed HTTP/2 stream reuse for 72% of requests for this site in last 24h. Some backend idle closes detected.

maria_cust: quick update — with comment keepalive every 20s stream persists beyond 5m. Looks much better.

josh_eng_runtime: good, that confirms idle-close race. We'll: (A) add an opt-in streaming keepalive header in runtime (RW-Stream-Keepalive: 20s) so SDKs can enable, (B) add a doc section recommending ALB idle >= 120s or use NLB for long-lived SSE, (C) file an engineering task to ensure writes that fail with EPIPE produce a graceful final event and consistent billing attribution.

priya_sre: I filed CLOUD-ALB-527 to track ALB timeout docs + infra checklist for Dedicated customers.

alex_support: escalated to eng-runtime with request id and pcap. Josh, assigning to you for the graceful-fail and header.

josh_eng_runtime: acked. I'll prototype RW-Stream-Keepalive in the next sprint, and a fallback that injects server-side comment heartbeats when enabled. Also will add better logging when write failures occur.

alex_support: thanks all. Maria, I'll follow up once eng has a patch and we have recommended config docs. Please dm me if the workaround fails. :thumbsup:
